 Recall Over 1.5 Million Pounds of Hotdogs, Other Meats Sold at Walmart and More Recalled. See the Full List
 Kayem Foods issued the recall after the company discovered an issue at a storage facility. Updated   Oct. 20, 2026, 1:17 PM EDT / Source : TODAY Sarah Jacoby
 Health Reporter
 Food Safety Concerns in the Spotlight Amid Recall Fatigue 02:32 Share Add TODAY to Google There’s a massive meat and poultry recall underway, which affects more than 1.5 million pounds of hotdogs, sausages, deli meats and bacon.
 Kayem Foods Inc. is voluntarily recalling the meat and poultry products, which were sold nationwide under brand names such as Kayem, Al Fresco, McKenzie, Triple M, Deutschmacher, Jordan’s and more. The recall comes after the company discovered a temperature issue at one of its storage facilities.
 In total, Kayem Foods is recalling “approximately 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat (RTE) meat and poultry products because they may have experienced temperature abuse during storage,” according to a recall announcement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service .
 The products were shipped to grocery stores and foodservice locations across the U.S. and in Hong Kong, the FSIS says.
 People who’ve purchased any of the recalled products should not eat them, the company urges.
 “Our business depends on providing consumers with safe food of the highest quality,” Matt Monkiewicz, Kayem Foods President and CEO, said in a statement . “Out of an abundance of caution, we are undertaking this voluntary recall.”
 “We take food safety very seriously and apologize to our valued consumers. Our management team takes full responsibility. We have learned from and corrected the issue and will not allow this to happen again,” the statement continued. 
 Which Products Are Being Recalled?
 The recall includes a massive list of meat and poultry products.
 All of the affected products were produced between March 31 and Oct. 7, 2026, the FSIS says. They have a wide range of expiration dates between May 2026 and February 2027.
 Additionally, products included in the recall will have establishment numbers EST. M/P 7839, EST. P 20935A or EST. M 9520 printed inside the USDA mark of inspection.
 Some of the products affected by the recall include:
 Kayem Old Tyme Beef & Pork Frankfurters, SKU#1003 UPC: 003077101003, expiration date Oct. 10, 2026.
 Kayem Fenway Franks, SKU# 1114 UPC: 003077101114, expiration dates Oct. 22 and Oct. 29, 2026.
 Kayem Slow Smoked Applewood Thick Cut Bacon, SKU# 1402 UPC: 003077101402, expiration dates between June 29 and Dec. 21, 2026.
 Al Fresco Spinach and Feta Chicken Sausage, SKU# 2631 UPC: 003077102631, expiration dates from Aug. 13 to Dec. 13, 2026.
 Al Fresco Roasted Garlic Chicken Sausage, SKU# 2632 UPC: 003077102632, expiration dates between July 26 and Dec. 13, 2026.
 Al Fresco Country Style Breakfast Chicken Sausage, SKU#2666 UPC: 003077102666, expiration dates from May 21 to Sept. 19, 2026.
 Triple M Chef’s Delight Tavern Ham, SKU#2977 UPC: 003077102977, expiration date Nov. 3, 2026.
 McKenzie Cob Smoked Uncured Bacon, SKU#9544 UPC: 003077109544, expiration dates between Aug. 2 and Nov. 25, 2026.
 McKenzie Black Forest Uncured Ham, SKU#9546 UPC: 003077109546, expiration dates from Oct. 16, 2026, to Jan. 28, 2027.
 McKenzie Oven Roasted Turkey Breast, SKU#9585 UPC: 075887809585, expiration dates from July 16 to Nov. 26, 2026.
 Deutschmacher Honey Ham, SKU# 9807 UPC: 003077109807, expiration dates between Aug. 13 and Nov. 12, 2026.
 Jordan’s Ball Game Treats, SKU# 9813 UPC: 003077109813, expiration date Oct. 17, 2026.
 Essem Frankfurts, SKU# 9813 UPC: 003077109813, expiration dates between Oct. 22 and Oct. 29, 2026. 
 Winnisimmet Slow Smoked Roasted Bacon, SKU# 9878 UPC: 003077109878, expiration dates between June 14 and Dec. 4, 2026.
 See the full list of recalled products on the FSIS site . You can also see photos of the products included in the recall here .
 Where Were the Recalled Meat and Poultry Products Sold?
 The recalled Kayem Foods hotdogs, sausages and other meat products were sold at major grocery retailers across the U.S.
 The FSIS does not list the specific stores or states where the products were sold. 
 However, Walmart is warning consumers that the affected products were sold in some of its stores in these states:
 Connecticut 
 Massachusetts 
 Maine 
 New Hampshire
 New York
 Pennsylvania
 Rhode Island 
 Vermont
 Why Are the Meat and Poultry Products Being Recalled?
 Kayem Foods is recalling the meat and poultry due to a temperature issue that occurred during storage. 
 The products are being recalled “due to the recent discovery of a cooling system malfunction at one of the company’s warehouses that resulted in storage temperature deviations,” the company explained in a statement. 
 The issue was discovered after a retail customer complained of “warm product temperatures” at the point of delivery on Oct. 1, the FSIS says. “The establishment investigated and determined that they stored various RTE meat and poultry products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations.”
 There have been no confirmed reports of illness related to eating any of the recalled products, the FSIS notes.
 What to Do If You Purchased Recalled Products
 If you purchased any of the recalled hotdogs, deli meats or other products, you should not eat them.
 Instead, dispose of them or return them to the place where you purchased them, the FSIS says. Additionally, you can contact Kayem Foods at the contact information on its website.
